Set B is slightly more faithful in the text condition for the radius claim, but this minor difference does not distinguish the overall quality given the shared major extraction failures.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractors systematically swapped the IDs and descriptions for beam details A1/A4 and B1/B4. This suggests a common failure mode in parsing the layout of the drawing labels versus the text layer.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain identical misbinding errors where Keynote labels (A1/A4 and B1/B4) are swapped with their corresponding grid locations, leading to incorrect label conditions and section properties for those beams. Set A is preferred because it extracts the full condition text for the beam opening radius ('around edges of openings in beams'), whereas Set B truncates it to 'around edges', making it vague.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets fail to correctly map Keynotes A1/A4 and B1/B4 to their grid locations (swapping them). Both also omit the Keynote ID 'E6' in the conditions for the Roof Beam claim (Claim 8 in A, Claim 7 in B), unlike other beam claims which include the Keynote ID.

baseline-first.note: Set A extracts 21 unique circuit claims correctly, covering the majority of the schedule, whereas Set B extracts only 5 claims. Set A suffers from 4 duplicate entries, but its completeness makes it far more useful for engineering review. Both sets miss the Main Breaker and several circuits at the bottom of the list (e.g., Guest Bedroom, Dryer, Water Heater, Inverter).
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss the Main Breaker (150A) and circuits 21-24, 29-32, 35-40. Set A's duplicates are exact repeats of earlier claims in the list, sometimes with minor variation in the condition label ('circuit' vs 'circuit number').

variant-first.note: Set A is better because it contains significantly fewer incorrect claims and no duplicates, whereas Set B propagates the OCR text layer's circuit number errors for most items and includes multiple duplicate claims. Both sets fail to verify circuit numbers against the image (which shows different numbers than the text layer for the middle section), but Set A's lower volume results in fewer total engineering errors. Set B's high error rate and redundancy make it less reliable despite higher coverage.
variant-first.remarks: The provided text layer has a systematic numbering shift for circuits 5-28 compared to the image (e.g., Image Circuit 5 is Text Layer Circuit 9). Both sets relied on the text layer numbers rather than the image, causing systematic misreads. Set B also duplicated 4 claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain identical extraction errors regarding the Wiring Schedule symbols: they misbind Symbol 151 to Symbol 10's data ('#12/2WG'), misbind Symbol 150 to Symbol 151's description ('ARMORED CABLE'), and extract Symbol 150's actual data under a vague 'cable' entity. Both also omit the Notes and annotations outside the schedule. Set A is slightly better because it uses the more precise attribute 'conductor material' for Wiring 150, whereas Set B uses the vague 'material'.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets fail to correctly map symbols 150, 151, and 10 from the text layer/image, likely due to layout confusion. Set B's use of 'material' instead of 'conductor material' is a minor quality degradation.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain identical engineering claims with the same significant misbinding errors regarding Wiring Schedule symbols 150, 151, and 10 (e.g., attributing Symbol 10's data to 151, and Symbol 151's description to 150). Both sets also omit the 'NOTES' section entirely and include a vague 'cable' entity claim. The only difference is a minor attribute naming inconsistency in Set A ('material' vs 'conductor material').
